prompt:
Writer Zitkala-Ša published essays, stories, and political writings in the early twentieth century. She also worked to protect Native rights and to preserve Dakota language and culture. Because her work crossed literary, musical, educational, and activist fields, scholars often describe her career as ______.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
explanation: The text says Zitkala-Ša worked across literary, musical, educational, and activist fields, so “varied” is most precise.

prompt:
Blue mussels are small shellfish that feed by filtering tiny particles from seawater. As they feed, they can remove some algae and suspended matter from the water. For this reason, large groups of mussels can sometimes improve water clarity in coastal areas.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Blue mussels can help make coastal water clearer by filtering particles as they feed.
choices.B: Blue mussels avoid living in coastal areas where algae are present.
choices.C: Seawater becomes cloudy only when shellfish stop feeding.
choices.D: Large groups of mussels prevent all algae from growing in the ocean.

explanation: The passage explains that mussels remove particles as they feed, which can improve water clarity.

prompt:
The schedule for the student film festival ______ three short documentaries and two animated films.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular subject “schedule” requires the singular verb “lists.”

prompt:
A student recorded the number of tickets sold for four school performances.
Performance | Tickets sold
Thursday matinee | 86
Friday evening | 124
Saturday matinee | 112
Saturday evening | 138
Which choice is supported by the data in the table?

choices.A: The Saturday evening performance sold the most tickets.
choices.B: The Thursday matinee sold more tickets than the Friday evening performance.
choices.C: The two matinee performances sold the same number of tickets.
choices.D: No performance sold more than 124 tickets.

explanation: Saturday evening sold 138 tickets, more than the other performances.

prompt:
At first, Priya thought the old family camera would be useless because its lens was scratched. But when she developed her first roll of film, she saw that the scratches created soft streaks of light around every window and streetlamp. Instead of replacing the camera, she began using it for night photographs.
Which choice best describes what happens in the text?

choices.A: Priya discovers that a flaw in the camera can create an effect she likes.
choices.B: Priya refuses to develop the film because the camera is old.
choices.C: Priya repairs the camera lens before taking any photographs.
choices.D: Priya decides that night photographs should never include light.

explanation: Priya first thinks the scratched lens is a problem but later uses the light streaks creatively.

prompt:
In a passage about early public clocks, a historian explains that clock towers were often placed in busy town centers. The historian adds, “Because many people did not own personal watches, a public clock helped workers, travelers, and shopkeepers coordinate their daily schedules.”
What is the main function of the quoted sentence?

choices.A: It explains why public clocks were useful to many people.
choices.B: It argues that shopkeepers were responsible for building clock towers.
choices.C: It describes the tools used to repair public clocks.
choices.D: It shows that personal watches were common in every household.

explanation: The quoted sentence explains that public clocks helped people without watches coordinate schedules.

prompt:
The town’s summer reading program includes book discussions and author visits. ______ it offers weekly storytelling sessions for younger children.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence adds another feature of the summer reading program.

prompt:
The student’s report discusses the vaquita, ______ small porpoise found in the Gulf of California.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: “Small porpoise” begins with a consonant sound, so “a” is correct.

prompt:
After the committee reviewed the proposal, ______ sent a revised version to the principal.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular pronoun “it” correctly refers to the proposal.

prompt:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mary Anning was a fossil collector in nineteenth-century England.
• She found important marine reptile fossils along the coast near Lyme Regis.
• Her discoveries helped scientists study prehistoric life.
• Anning had limited formal scientific recognition during her lifetime.
• Today she is often discussed as an important figure in paleontology.
The student wants to introduce Anning and explain the importance of her discoveries. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?

choices.A: Mary Anning, a nineteenth-century fossil collector, found marine reptile fossils that helped scientists study prehistoric life.
choices.B: Mary Anning lived near Lyme Regis, a coastal area in England.
choices.C: Fossil collectors sometimes search along cliffs, beaches, and rocky shorelines.
choices.D: Mary Anning received limited formal scientific recognition during her lifetime.

explanation: This choice introduces Anning and explains why her discoveries mattered.

prompt:
The new cafeteria menu includes several vegetarian meals. ______ students who do not eat meat now have more lunch options.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: More lunch options for students who do not eat meat is an effect of adding vegetarian meals.

explanation: Sentence 3 gives specific examples of how students can use the measurements introduced in sentence 2.

prompt:

prompt:

prompt:
Some communities create “little free pantries,” small outdoor boxes where people can leave or take canned food, soap, and other basic supplies. Because the pantries are open throughout the day, they can provide quick access to needed items without requiring a formal appointment.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Little free pantries can make basic supplies more accessible to community members.
choices.B: Little free pantries are used only to store items that no one needs.
choices.C: Communities build little free pantries mainly to replace grocery stores completely.
choices.D: Outdoor boxes cannot be used to share canned food or soap.

explanation: The passage explains that pantries provide quick access to basic supplies throughout the day.

prompt:
Botanists studying water lilies note that the plants have broad, flat leaves that float on the surface of ponds. These leaves can capture sunlight while also spreading the plant’s weight across the water.
According to the text, what is one function of water lilies’ broad, flat leaves?

choices.A: They help the plants capture sunlight at the water’s surface.
choices.B: They allow the plants to grow only in dry soil.
choices.C: They prevent ponds from containing any other plants.
choices.D: They help the plants move quickly from one pond to another.

explanation: The text says the leaves float on the surface and capture sunlight.

prompt:
A student is revising the following sentence.
The school launched a lunchtime tutoring table, and students can visit it to ask questions, review homework, or study for quizzes.

choices.A: The school launched a lunchtime tutoring table where students can ask questions, review homework, or study for quizzes.
choices.B: The school launched a lunchtime tutoring table, students can visit it to ask questions, review homework, or study for quizzes.
choices.C: The school launched a lunchtime tutoring table and asking questions, reviewing homework, or studying for quizzes.
choices.D: The school launched a lunchtime tutoring table because students, questions, homework, and quizzes.

explanation: This choice combines the ideas clearly and avoids a comma splice.

prompt:
